clues.text: This small town is in Chad, in the Wadi Fira part of the land. It has its own court and is served by an airport.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside Chad's Wadi Fira region

source.quote: Iriba (Arabic: هريبا) is a small town in the Wadi Fira Region of Chad. It is known as part of the Kobé Department as well as having its own prefecture and area court. It is currently being served by the Iriba Airport.

clues.text: This desert town has two clear times of year, dry and wet. Rain falls, then soon runs off in short-lived streams, while summer heat stays fierce and dry.
clues.narrowing: rules out desert towns without a sharp dry and rainy split and fierce dry summers

source.quote: Iriba has a desert climate with two distinct periods, dry and rainy seasons. During the rainy season, considerable rainfall occurs in the area, which disappears rapidly in the seasonal rivers named "Wadi". The winters (from December to February) can be quite cold, and the summertime is extremely hot and dry, with water shortage being a chronic problem in the area.

clues.text: In the year 2004, a large wave of people fled the Darfur area and came to this town's lands. Most were of the same folk group as the town's own people.
clues.narrowing: rules out towns with no large 2004 influx of people fleeing Darfur

source.quote: A large number of the refugees fled from the Darfur area to the general vicinity of Iriba in the year 2004. The refugees are mainly from the same ethnicity and live in three large refugee camps in the area; namely Iridimi, Touloum, and Amnabak.

clues.text: Three big camps near this town hold more than sixty thousand folks who fled their homes. World aid groups work there to help and keep them safe.
clues.narrowing: leaves only the town ringed by three camps holding over sixty thousand displaced people

source.quote: The three camps accommodate over sixty thousand refugees. The refugee influx required extensive international presence for assistance and protection of the displaced population. UNHCR is the leading international agency in the area while WFP and many other NGOs help with the different aspects of life for the refugees.

clues.text: The local folk are the Zaghawa, who live on both sides of the line with Sudan. They speak their own tongue and still look to their own Sultan as their chief.
clues.narrowing: confirms the Chad town whose Zaghawa people also live across the Sudan border

source.quote: The ethnicity of the Iriban people is referred to as "Zaghawa". The ethnic group lives on both sides of the border in Chad and Sudan, with the local language being Zaghawa, a Nilo-Saharan language. The formal languages of the area are Arabic and French. The Zaghawas have their traditional leadership, under the Sultan of Zaghawa.
